Multivariate data are common in the environmental sciences, occurring whenever we measure several response variables from each replicate sample (for example, the abundances of many species). These pages cover:

* [Model-based analysis of multivariate abundance data](MVabund.qmd) with mvabund
* Grouping samples by their similarity with [cluster analysis](cluster-analysis.qmd)
* Summarising many variables into a few with [principal components analysis](pca.qmd)
* Representing relationships among samples with [multidimensional scaling](mds.qmd)

For other ways of plotting multivariate data, see [Visualising multivariate data](../data-visualisation/data-visualisation.qmd#visualising-multivariate-data).

This part also covers [generalised additive models](generalised-additive-models.qmd) (GAMs) for non-linear relationships, [forecasting with time series](time-series-analysis.qmd), and meta-analysis:

* [Meta-analyses 1](meta-analysis.qmd#introduction): Introduction and calculating effect sizes  
* [Meta-analyses 2](meta-analysis.qmd#fixed-effect-and-random-effect-models): Fixed effect and random effect models  
* [Meta-analyses 3](meta-analysis.qmd#multilevel-models): More complex models
